introduction.p: An increasing sequence bounded above converges to the supremum of its terms. A decreasing sequence bounded below converges to their infimum. This section proves both statements from the least-upper-bound property.

subsection.title: Monotone sequences
subsection.p: A sequence is monotone if it is increasing or decreasing.

example.title: Example
example.p: It is bounded above by 1. The terms approach 1.

example.title: Example
example.p: It is bounded below by 0. The terms approach 0.

subsection.title: The theorem

statement.p: If an increasing sequence is bounded above, then it converges.
If a decreasing sequence is bounded below, then it converges.

subsection.p: The theorem is not saying that every sequence converges. It is saying that two conditions together force convergence:

paragraphs.title: Proof sketch
paragraphs.p: The sequence L_n is increasing and bounded above by R_1, so it converges. The sequence R_n is decreasing and bounded below by L_1, so it converges.
Thus the left and right endpoints squeeze down to one number.
